scenarios.title: Keep an earlier report while the application changes
scenarios.summary: Create a point-in-time view, run a supplied update, and compare earlier and current data.
scenarios.objective: Prepare report/before_run before applying Next report. Use 128 KiB chunks and reserve 1–2 MiB of COW space. Current status must be week2=ok and total count=24; before_run must retain the supplied earlier values of both records. Keep at least 6 MiB free in report. Keep the origin allocation, reference volume, foreign device and unrelated data unchanged. Do not leave extra snapshots.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare current records, saved records, validity and physical reservations separately. A new matching name does not restore old history. Refused operations retain prior work; reset only this attempt if an essential original view was lost.

updates.label: Next report
updates.explanation: The application writes two current records. A previously created saved view must still read the earlier report.

lesson.prerequisite_note: First complete linear LVM growth and allocation practice: identify PV, VG, LV and free physical extents. This simulator supplies fixed-size raw application records, not a mounted filesystem. You do not need a real device or mount.

concepts.title: A saved view is a point in time
concepts.text: The origin is the current application data. A snapshot lets you read an earlier view while the application keeps writing. Create it before the change you want protection from; a later snapshot cannot invent earlier data.

concepts.title: Copy on the first write
concepts.text: Copy-on-write (COW) saves a chunk’s old bytes the first time the origin writes there. Unchanged chunks still read from the origin. Rewriting a copied chunk does not consume another chunk in that snapshot.

concepts.title: Separate physical space
concepts.text: The origin address range and its COW reservation are different storage. The example reserves a raw LV for the saved chunks and leaves the reference LV intact. Inspect vgs for the remaining physical space.

concepts.title: What you can inspect here
concepts.text: These exercises use fixed-size, printable text records in raw virtual storage. The record reader and application-update buttons are simulator tools, not mounts, filesystems or Linux utilities. This is not a backup independent of the origin.

lesson.description: sample/report starts with status demo1=ok and total count=03. Reserve sample/before_run first. Next report changes current data to demo2=ok and count=09; the saved view still reads demo1=ok and count=03.

lesson.try_change: After the worked example, create a spare saved view and check again: the extra storage violates the handover requirement. Remove only spare and retry. Reset and apply Next report before creating before_run to see why timing matters.

scenarios.title: Prevent a saved view from exhausting its COW space
scenarios.summary: Diagnose the copied-chunk budget and grow the saved store before the scheduled update.
scenarios.objective: Grow budget/rolling while it is still readable to 2–3 MiB of COW space, preserving its existing point in time and 128 KiB chunks. Apply Scheduled eight chunks. The first eight current records must contain their supplied new values; the other eight current records must stay at their original values. rolling must retain all sixteen original records and remain readable. Keep at least 8 MiB free in budget and preserve all origin, reference and device allocations. Do not leave extra snapshots.

updates.label: Scheduled eight chunks
updates.explanation: Eight distinct 128 KiB chunks change. The initial 1 MiB COW store has room for only seven data chunks in this exercise.

updates.label: Unexpected eight more chunks
updates.explanation: Eight additional distinct chunks change. A 2 MiB COW reservation has fifteen data chunks after the exercise metadata allowance; sixteen distinct copied chunks exhaust it.

lesson.prerequisite_note: First complete linear LVM growth and allocation practice: identify PV, VG, LV and free physical extents. This simulator supplies fixed-size raw application records, not a mounted filesystem. You do not need a real device or mount.

concepts.title: Plan before the write
concepts.text: A classic COW snapshot needs room for distinct chunks that change, not just a count of edited records. Records sharing one chunk share its first-write cost; repeated writes to the same chunk reuse the saved bytes.

concepts.title: Calculate this exercise’s budget
concepts.text: Chunks are 128 KiB here. One chunk is reserved for metadata as a teaching convention: 1 MiB holds seven data chunks, and 2 MiB holds fifteen. Real LVM metadata accounting differs; do not use these numbers as a production sizing rule.

concepts.title: Grow the saved store, not the origin
concepts.text: Use lvextend on the still-valid snapshot store before its space runs out. Physical extents must be free in the same group. The application origin stays 2 MiB; expanding it does not add COW space.

concepts.title: Once invalid, old data is unavailable
concepts.text: If a new write needs more COW chunks than fit, the snapshot becomes invalid and old data is unavailable. The origin write still succeeds. Extending an invalid snapshot does not revive it. Reset practice to retry planning; a new snapshot means a new time.

lesson.description: practice/rolling starts readable with 1 MiB reserved. Eight distinct 128 KiB chunks will change. Grow it to 2 MiB first, then apply Scheduled eight chunks. The current first eight records read new values; rolling still reads all sixteen old values.

updates.label: Scheduled eight chunks
updates.explanation: Eight distinct 128 KiB chunks change. The initial 1 MiB COW store has room for only seven data chunks in this exercise.

updates.label: Unexpected eight more chunks
updates.explanation: Eight additional distinct chunks change. A 2 MiB COW reservation has fifteen data chunks after the exercise metadata allowance; sixteen distinct copied chunks exhaust it.

worked.explanation: Increase the still-readable rolling COW store to 2 MiB before the application writes. Leave the 2 MiB origin and reference volume unchanged.
Apply Scheduled eight chunks. Eight copied chunks now fit; inspect the current record, saved value and remaining physical reserve.

lesson.try_change: After the 2 MiB worked example, apply Unexpected eight more chunks. Sixteen distinct copied chunks exceed fifteen available data chunks: rolling becomes invalid while current writes succeed. Reset to retry. Also reset and apply Scheduled eight chunks before growth to see the original sizing failure.

scenarios.title: Repair a damaged import and hand over a verified saved view
scenarios.summary: Use a readable source, preserve its identity, retire an invalid view, and verify a fresh handover.
scenarios.objective: Repair recovery/report row0 and row1 using their original trusted saved values. Keep the original recovery/trusted snapshot readable, at its supplied 2 MiB size and 128 KiB chunks. Retire only recovery/expired. After repairing the current records, create recovery/handover with 128 KiB chunks and 1–2 MiB COW space; its row0 and row1 must match trusted. Leave every other current record, origin allocation, reference volume and device unchanged. Keep at least 8 MiB free in recovery. Do not leave extra snapshots.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Compare current records, saved records, validity and physical reservations separately. A new matching name does not restore old history. Refused operations retain prior work; reset only this attempt if an essential original view was lost.

updates.label: Repeat damaged import
updates.explanation: This explicit simulator workload overwrites the two restored current records. Compare them with the trusted saved values before repairing.

lesson.prerequisite_note: First complete linear LVM growth and allocation practice: identify PV, VG, LV and free physical extents. This simulator supplies fixed-size raw application records, not a mounted filesystem. You do not need a real device or mount.

concepts.title: Diagnose which view is usable
concepts.text: A snapshot marked invalid cannot supply the missing old bytes. The supplied trusted view is still readable. Compare current and saved records before deciding what to copy; never assume every snapshot is useful.

concepts.title: Restore only the requested records
concepts.text: The simulated application reader can copy one saved record to current storage. This is a deliberate simulator tool, not a Linux command, filesystem restore or lvconvert merge. Leave unrelated records and the reference LV untouched.

concepts.title: Names cannot replace old history
concepts.text: Keep the original trusted object. Removing it and creating another snapshot with that name gives a new point in time, even if some bytes happen to match. The checks retain the supplied snapshot’s identity.

concepts.title: Verify the handover after the repair
concepts.text: Retire only the expired COW store, and create handover after the record repair. Read both restored records through the new view. Verify free group space and protected data as well as a success message.

lesson.description: training/report has two damaged current records. trusted still reads the good values; expired is invalid. Copy trusted row0 and row1 into current data, retire expired, then create handover. Inspect handover rather than trusting its name.

updates.label: Repeat damaged import
updates.explanation: This explicit simulator workload overwrites the two restored current records. Compare them with the trusted saved values before repairing.

worked.explanation: Inspect trusted row0, then explicitly copy that saved record into the current application. This is a simulator operation, not an LVM merge command.
Select row1 and copy its trusted saved value too. Other current records must remain unchanged.
Remove only the expired COW store. It is invalid; adding space cannot recover its old bytes. Keep the original trusted point.
Create handover after both copies. Inspect its two records and check the protected neighbor and remaining reserve.

lesson.try_change: After the worked handover, apply Repeat damaged import. Read the changed current records and both saved views. Copy only the two trusted records again, check, and confirm the original trusted object was retained.
